601: A family is like a lamp that should never go out. But when the dirt of laziness builds up on it, its light fades and dies.
602: If you want your family to rise and be truly respected, treat laziness as something deadly and get rid of it in the way you live.
603: When a foolish person holds on to laziness, which destroys everything, the family they were born into is ruined even before they die.
604: When people fall into laziness and make no real effort, their family's good name falls apart and their faults keep growing.
605: Putting things off, forgetting, laziness and too much sleep are four things people headed for ruin love. They are like a pleasure boat that carries them to disaster.
606: Even if lazy people get the riches of kings who ruled the whole earth, they will rarely get any real good out of it.
607: People who give in to laziness and make no real effort will end up hearing harsh scolding and mocking words.
608: If laziness settles into someone from a respected family, it will end up making them a slave to their own enemies.
609: When a person gets rid of the laziness that rules them, the faults that had crept into their family and their own strength will disappear.
610: A king who is never lazy will win, all at once, the whole world that the god who measured the worlds with his steps walked across.
611: Never give up by telling yourself a task is too hard. Effort itself gives you the strength and greatness to get it done.
612: Once you start a task, be careful not to let your effort drop. The world leaves behind people who leave their work half-done.
613: Being proud that you can help others depends on one thing only: the good habit of working hard.
614: A person who will not work but wants to give generously will fail, like a sword waved around by a coward who is afraid to fight.
615: A person who wants to work more than they want fun becomes like a pillar for their family. They wipe away the family's troubles and hold them up.
616: Effort brings riches and success. Not making an effort brings poverty.
617: People say the dark goddess of bad luck lives with the lazy. The goddess of good fortune, who sits on a lotus, lives with the hard work of someone who is not lazy.
618: Having bad luck is nothing to be ashamed of. The real shame is knowing what needs to be done and still not making the effort.
619: Even if fate stops you from reaching your goal, your effort will still pay you back for all your hard work.
620: People who keep working hard without giving up or slowing down will even see fate turn around and run away from them.
621: When trouble comes, smile at it. Nothing beats trouble as well as staying cheerful and calm.
622: Even trouble as huge as a flood goes away once a wise person thinks about it with a steady mind.
623: People who do not let trouble make them sad turn things around. They end up making trouble itself suffer.
624: Some people are like an ox that keeps pulling a cart through every rut and muddy patch. The trouble that meets them is the one that ends up suffering.
625: Even if troubles come one on top of another, a person who does not break down inside will make those troubles themselves end up in trouble.
626: People who never held on tightly to their riches, saying 'we have it,' will not cry 'we have lost it all' when it is gone.
627: Great people know the body is just a target for pain. So they do not treat the worry that pain brings as a disaster.
628: A person who does not chase after pleasure, and who accepts that hard times are a normal part of life, never really falls into misery.
629: A person who does not get carried away by fun in good times will not be crushed by sadness in bad times.
630: If a person can take hard times as if they were good times, they will win a kind of greatness that even their enemies admire and wish they had.
631: A good minister (an adviser to the king) is excellent at planning the tools needed, the right time, the way to do it, and the hard task itself.
632: A good minister is also excellent in five more things: firm courage, protecting the people, learning, understanding, and hard work.
633: A good minister knows how to pull allies away from the enemy, keep their own side loyal, and win back people who have left.
634: A good minister can study a problem carefully, act only after choosing wisely, and give a firm, clear answer.
635: The best person to plan with is someone who knows what is right, speaks with deep knowledge and care, and always knows how to get things done.
636: When a person has a naturally sharp mind and also learning from books, what clever trick could ever beat them?
637: Even when you know from books how to do something, act only after you understand how the world really works.
638: Even if the king ignores good advice and does not know better himself, the adviser by his side still has the duty to tell him what is truly good.
639: Seventy crores (seven hundred million) of enemies are better than one minister at your side who secretly plans to harm you.
640: People without the skill to get things done will leave their work unfinished, even when they have planned it the right way.
641: The gift of speaking well is a treasure all by itself. It is not just one of the many other good things a person may have.
642: Both success and ruin can come from what we say. So be very careful never to make a slip in your speech.
643: Good speech holds listeners tightly, and it is spoken so well that even people who have not heard it want to hear it.
644: Speak only after you understand the people listening. Nothing does more good or brings more gain than speech that fits its listeners.
645: Say what you have to say only after making sure no one can give a better answer that beats your words.
646: Speaking so that others want to listen, and picking out the useful points from what others say, is the way of people with no faults.
647: It is hard for anyone to beat a person in an argument when that person speaks powerfully, never slips up, and is not afraid.
648: If the world finds people who can speak in an orderly and pleasant way, it will quickly do what they ask.
649: People who do not know how to say a few words without faults are surely the ones who love to say many words.
650: People who cannot explain what they have learned so others understand it are like flowers that bloom in bunches but have no smell.
651: Good helpers can bring a person success, but good actions bring everything a person could want.
652: Always stay away from any action that brings neither a good name nor any real good.
653: People who say 'we want to rise higher' must stay away from any action that would dim their good name.
654: People who see clearly and are not shaken will never do anything shameful, even when they are in deep trouble.
655: Do not do anything that will later make you cry, 'What have I done!' And if you have already done such a thing, it is best not to do it again.
656: Even if you have to watch your own mother go hungry, do not do anything that wise people would call wrong.
657: For good people, being very poor is better than getting rich in a shameful way.
658: People who do the things the wise have told them not to do will suffer for it, even if those things work out.
659: Everything gained by making others cry will be lost and leave you crying. Things gained in good ways may be lost for a while, but they will pay off later.
660: Trying to keep yourself safe with money gained by cheating is like pouring water into a pot of wet, unbaked clay and hoping it holds.
661: Being firm in action really means being firm in mind. Every other kind of strength is something different.
662: People who have studied this say firm action follows two rules: stay away from harm before it comes, and do not give up when it comes anyway.
663: Real skill means keeping a task quiet until it is finished. If people learn about it halfway, it can cause trouble that cannot be fixed.
664: Anyone can talk about how to do something. The hard part is doing it exactly the way it was said.
665: The firm action of people who have become great reaches even the king, and so everyone comes to respect it.
666: If people who make plans stay firm in carrying them out, they will get what they planned, and in just the way they planned it.
667: Never look down on someone because of how small or plain they look. Some people are like the tiny pin that holds the wheel on a huge rolling chariot.
668: Once you have clearly decided what to do, do it without wavering and without delay.
669: Even if a lot of hardship comes your way, keep going bravely with work that will bring happiness in the end.
670: No matter what other strengths they have, the world does not value people who do not value being firm in action.
671: The goal of thinking things over is to reach a firm decision. Once you have decided, letting that decision sit and wait is harmful.
672: Take your time with tasks that should be done slowly. But never delay tasks that must be done right away.
673: Whenever you can act directly, that is best. When you cannot, find another way that will work and do it that way.
674: Think about it: an unfinished task and an enemy not fully beaten are like leftover sparks of a fire. They can grow back and destroy you.
675: Before you act, think clearly about five things until nothing is unclear: money, tools, timing, the task itself, and the place.
676: Act only after looking at what it takes to finish the task, the problems that may come up along the way, and the gain it will bring at the end.
677: The right way to do a task is to find out what someone who knows that task well thinks about it.
678: Using one task to get another one done is like using a trained elephant to catch a wild one.
679: Winning over people who are not yet on your side is more urgent than doing good things for people who are already your friends.
680: Leaders of a small country, afraid that their own people are scared, will give in to a stronger power and accept peace if they are offered a chance.
681: An envoy (a messenger sent to speak for a king) should be loving, come from a respected family, and have the good manners that kings value.
682: Love for the king, knowing what is good for him, and the skill of choosing the right words are three things an envoy must have.
683: A person who goes before kings with spears to speak for their own king's success must be the most skilled scholar even among the learned.
684: Send a person on the mission only if they have three things together: good sense, a fine appearance, and learning that has been tested.
685: A good envoy sums things up briefly, leaves out harsh words, speaks so pleasantly that people smile, and so brings good to their king.
686: A good envoy is well-learned, is not scared by angry looks, speaks so the message sinks in, and knows what is right for the moment.
687: The best envoy knows their duty, waits for the right time, chooses the right place, and thinks carefully before speaking.
688: A person who carries the king's message exactly as given must be honest and clean, have good helpers, be brave, and above all tell the truth.
689: Only a person strong enough never to let a shameful word slip out should carry their king's message to other kings.
690: A true envoy delivers the king's whole message and works for the king's good, holding nothing back, even if it costs the envoy their life.
691: People who serve moody, powerful kings should act like people warming themselves by a fire. They should not go too far away or too close.
692: If you do not want the things the king himself wants, the king will give you success that lasts.
693: If you want to stay safe, avoid serious mistakes. Once the king becomes suspicious of you, no one can make him trust you again.
694: When you are with great and powerful people, do not whisper in someone's ear or share a secret smile with anyone.
695: When the king is talking in secret, do not try to listen in or ask him about it. Hear the secret only if he chooses to tell you.
696: Understand the king's mood, wait for the right time, and then say what is needed in a pleasant way he will want to hear.
697: Tell the king things that are worth wanting. Never speak of useless things, even if he asks you to.
698: Do not look down on the king, thinking 'he is younger than me' or 'he is my relative.' Act with respect for the high place he holds.
699: People with steady judgment never think 'the king likes us' and then do things the king would not accept.
700: Being too relaxed because 'we are old friends of the king,' and then behaving badly, will lead a person to ruin.
701: A person who can look at someone and know what they mean without a word being said is always a jewel to this world surrounded by the sea.
702: A person who can know without any doubt what is inside someone else's mind should be thought of as equal to a god.
703: People who can read what others mean from the signs on their face are worth getting as helpers, whatever you have to give to win them.
704: People who understand what others mean without being told, and people who cannot, may look the same, but they are very different.
705: If your eyes cannot read what someone means from the signs they give, what use are your eyes among all the parts of your body?
706: Just as clear crystal shows the color of whatever is next to it, the face shows whatever is strongest in the heart.
707: Is anything smarter than the face? Whether a person is happy or angry, the face shows it first.
708: If you have people who can look into your heart and understand what has happened to you, it is enough to stand where they can see your face.
709: To people who understand the different ways eyes look, the eyes alone will show if someone is an enemy or a friend.
710: If you look closely at people who say they can read others well, you will find their only measuring stick is the eyes. They use nothing else.
711: People with clean minds who know the power of words should first understand the group they are speaking to, and then speak with care.
712: Good people who know how words work should choose the right moment, understand the subject fully, and only then speak.
713: People who start speaking without understanding their listeners do not know how words work. They have no real skill at all.
714: Among bright, learned people, show how bright you are. Among dull people, be plain like a white-painted wall and do not show off.
715: Of all good things, the best is holding back from speaking first when you are among elders who are wiser than you.
716: Making a mistake in speech in front of people who understand many subjects is like slipping and falling off the right path.
717: The learning of people who have studied deeply shines brightest among those who can judge words without any mistakes.
718: Speaking to people who can understand is like watering a garden bed where plants are already growing.
719: People who can speak good things well to a good group should never, even by mistake, speak about them to a low-minded group.
720: Speaking to people who are not like-minded is like spilling amrita (the drink that makes gods live forever) into a dirty drain.
721: People with pure minds who know the power of words and understand their listeners will not stumble when they speak before a powerful group.
722: People who can share what they have learned with other learned people, in a way that really reaches them, are called the most learned of all.
723: Many people are ready to die fighting among enemies. Few people can stand in front of a group and speak without fear.
724: Share what you have learned with learned people so it reaches them. Then learn from those who know more the things you do not yet know.
725: Study the right way to reason and argue, so that you can answer questions in front of a group without fear.
726: What use is a sword to someone who is not brave? What use are books to someone afraid of a group of sharp thinkers?
727: The learning of someone who is afraid to speak in front of a group is like a shiny sword in the hand of a coward facing the enemy.
728: No matter how many subjects they have studied, people who cannot share good things clearly with a good group are of no use.
729: People who have studied and understood, yet are afraid to speak before a group of good people, are said to be even lower than people who never learned.
730: People who fear a group and so cannot share what they have learned in a way that reaches others are like the dead, even though they are alive.
731: A true country has three things together: crops that never fail, good and worthy people, and rich people whose riches do not shrink.
732: A true country is so rich that others want it, is free from terrible disasters, and grows plenty of crops.
733: A true country can carry heavy burdens that fall on it all at once, and still pay its ruler all the taxes it owes.
734: A true country carries on free from terrible hunger, diseases that never end, and enemies that destroy.
735: A true country has no groups fighting each other, no enemies inside who bring ruin, and no killer gangs that trouble the king.
736: Wise people say the best country is one that never meets ruin, and even when harm does come, does not lose its riches.
737: The parts of a country are water from rain and from springs, hills in the right places, rivers that flow from them, and a strong fort.
738: Wise people say a country has five jewels: no disease, riches, good crops, happiness and safety.
739: Wise people say a true country is one whose riches come without having to search for them. A land that gives riches only after hard searching is not a true country.
740: Even if a land has all these good things, it is of no use if it does not have a good king who gets along with his people.
741: A fort is a treasure both for a king who goes out to attack and for a king who stays inside it to protect himself out of fear.
742: A true fort has water as clear as a jewel, open land, hills, and a forest with thick shade.
743: Books on this subject say a fort's wall must have four things: height, thickness, strength, and be hard to get to.
744: A fort should have only a few places that need guarding but lots of room inside, and it should crush the spirit of any enemy that attacks.
745: A fort should be hard to capture, full of stored food, and easy for the people inside to defend.
746: A true fort has everything that may be needed, and good, brave soldiers who will help when danger comes.
747: A true fort cannot be taken by surrounding it, by attacking it directly, or by tricks from people inside.
748: A true fort lets the people inside, holding their ground, beat even a strong army that is skilled at surrounding forts.
749: A true fort becomes famous because its fighters are so skilled that they knock down the enemy right at the front line.
750: No matter how great a fort is, it is no fort at all if the people in it are not skilled and strong in action.
